title: Why Adoption Stalls — and How to Change the Motion

lessons.learned: Customers get stuck below the concept layer
lessons.change: Run design sessions as decision-conversion sessions. Capture: decision, owner, rationale, constraint, next test.
lessons.example: "Decision needed: migration unit = app/module/component; owner = Gary; test = apply to one real build path."

lessons.learned: Workshops teach mechanics but don't change behavior
lessons.change: End every workshop with a working surface, not slides: repo, spec, prompt files, decision log, next tasks.
lessons.example: After Agentic SDLC workshop, leave a repo where Copilot can generate issues from the real Honeywell spec.

lessons.learned: Adoption stalls when Copilot has no system to work against
lessons.change: Build a Copilot-addressable project system: specs, constraints, decisions, open questions, task paths.
lessons.example: Copilot reads the spec repo and asks specific questions about build artifacts instead of giving generic advice.

lessons.learned: Meetings repeat because context is fragmented
lessons.change: Start each follow-up from the system: what changed, what is open, what was decided. Update it live.
lessons.example: "Last time we decided X, left Y open, need to resolve Z today." Update the repo during the call.

lessons.change: Coach the customer to query, update, and improve the system themselves. Success = customer self-service.
lessons.example: Gary updates planning in the repo via Copilot, then starts two more projects without needing Microsoft.

bottomLine: The change is not fewer design sessions. It is changing design sessions from advice delivery into system-building.
